summary: The submission is a polished, working travel-journal globe. Six locally loaded trips cover six continents; list, globe-marker, and clustered-marker selection all open synchronized trip details with highlighted locations. Filters, chronological view, empty-state recovery, reset-with-filter-preservation, shareable URL reload, and back navigation work. Valid real-time 3D is evident from the rotating globe's changing geography, marker occlusion, and spatial highlight changes. The 390px layout remains readable and exposes the controls, though keyboard activation and reduced-motion camera behavior were not directly exercised within the call budget.

runtime.reason: The page loaded at 1440x900 with the Meridian title, full interface, and WebGL globe. All application and photo resources in the network log returned 200; the only console error was a nonblocking missing favicon.ico (404).

scene.reason: The scene is a genuine interactive 3D globe rather than a static image: coastlines, lighting, surface shading, depth, and marker projections remain spatially coherent as the camera changes between Europe/Africa, Asia, and the Americas views.

checks.reason: Three distinct views show real depth and changing geometry: the initial Europe/Africa hemisphere, the Banff-focused Americas hemisphere, and a dragged Asia-centered view. Markers move with the sphere and far-side markers disappear behind it.

Composition, typography, color, and materials form a coherent editorial field-journal presentation. The cream archive panel, dark globe, green landmasses, and orange markers maintain clear hierarchy and legibility across desktop and mobile.

Primary UI actions produce meaningful feedback: selecting Kyoto from the list, Banff from its globe marker, and Lisbon from the nearby-trips popup each opened the corresponding article, updated the URL, and focused/highlighted the matching globe location.

Repeat and recovery flows work: combined search and year filtering reduced the archive to one result, a conflicting combination produced an explanatory empty state with a clear recovery action, timeline mode ordered trips newest to oldest, reset restored the full globe without clearing filters, and share/refresh/back navigation restored coherent journal context.

Desktop 1440x900 and mobile 390x844 layouts were inspected. The mobile full-page view keeps the globe, filter controls, all six trip entries, lower reset control, and footer content visible and readable. Reload preserved the direct trip URL. Network resources were healthy; the sole console issue was a nonblocking favicon 404.

The six-entry archive covers Europe, Asia, North America, Africa, Oceania, and South America. Each list entry exposes a locally bundled photo with meaningful alt text, specific dates, country, continent, and a diary summary; opened details for Kyoto, Banff, and Patagonia include full diary text and geographic coordinates. The network log confirms all six local JPEG assets loaded with 200 responses.

List and globe selection open the same journal context and matching highlight. Kyoto selected from the list opened Trip 02 and focused the Kyoto marker; Banff selected from its map marker opened Trip 03 and moved the globe to North America; the cluster-selected Lisbon opened Trip 01. Markers are placed consistently with the listed coordinates and continent.

Far-side trip markers are not exposed or selectable in the tested views; only markers on the visible hemisphere appear. The nearby Lisbon and Marrakech markers are disambiguated by a two-item popup, and each button independently selects its trip.

Search and year filters combine correctly, timeline mode is chronological (2025 to 2023), and zero matches produce a useful 'Nothing pinned here' explanation with a clear-search-and-year recovery action. After orbiting the camera with a lake/2024 filter active, Reset view restored the full globe while the active search and year remained unchanged.

A direct #trip=patagonia URL was loaded and reloaded; it restored Trip 06/06, the Patagonia article, coordinates, and map focus. Browser back returned to the root journal with all six journeys and Timeline mode still selected. The duplicate same-URL navigation used for the refresh required one extra back step but did not lose journal context.

All six trips are exposed as native buttons in the accessibility tree, and the 390px full-page layout is readable with ordinary document content below the globe and explicit vertical-scroll guidance on the canvas. However, actual Tab/Enter activation of every list item and the reduced-motion camera transition were not directly exercised within the call budget, so these aspects remain only partially verified.

instruction.reason: Core requested flows and content are delivered coherently, including trip synchronization, geographic placement, clustered markers, filtering, chronological view, empty-state recovery, reset behavior, shareable URLs, and back navigation. The score stops short of 4 because keyboard activation and reduced-motion camera handling were not directly verified.

spatial.reason: The globe consistently behaves as a sphere across multiple viewpoints. Continents and markers stay geographically coherent, near-side markers remain visible, far-side markers are occluded, and the selected location is highlighted without spatial contradictions.

interaction.reason: The primary flows, combinations, and recovery behavior are reliable: list and marker selection, cluster disambiguation, filtering, empty-state recovery, timeline switching, reset without filter loss, direct-trip reload, and back navigation all produced the expected visible state changes.

visual.reason: The distressed editorial typography, restrained cream and dark-green palette, map linework, photography, and orange pin accents consistently support the field-journal concept. Hierarchy remains clear in the desktop detail view, timeline, empty state, and mobile stacked layout.

stability.reason: Tested desktop, mobile, reload, filtering, selection, and history flows remained usable. Application and photo assets loaded successfully, but the console contains a nonblocking favicon 404, and one automated cluster-button click timed out because the animated marker was not stable while the camera settled.

limitations: The 40-call budget prevented a direct Tab/Enter pass through every trip button and an emulated prefers-reduced-motion camera-transition test; T06 is therefore marked PARTIAL.
Mobile evaluation used a 390x844 viewport rather than real touch hardware. The full-page render and scroll guidance confirm a scrollable document, but no physical touch gesture was performed.

Coordinates and full diary text were opened directly for Kyoto, Banff, and Patagonia; the other three entries were verified from list metadata, local photo assets, and consistently structured selection UI rather than individually opened detail panels.
No export/download control was present or advertised, so no downloaded-export flow applied.
Console and network diagnostics are recorded in evidence/console.txt and evidence/network.txt; they are not included in screenshot evidence arrays.
